title: Rowan: specific enforcement in French contract law
summary: The assigned comparative reading explains French specific enforcement, substitute performance, and limits based on impossibility or manifest disproportion.
notes:
The reading places the revised Civil Code provisions in the context of earlier French law and distinguishes performance in kind from monetary compensation. It examines Article 1221, including the significance of good faith and the comparison between the cost to the debtor and the creditor’s interest. It also discusses Article 1222’s route for arranging performance by another and the coercive payment mechanism known as an astreinte.

These mechanisms serve different functions. A coercive payment intended to induce compliance is not simply the same measure as damages for loss. Compare the source’s institutional and remedial assumptions with Klein and Walgreen, and preserve its distinctions between versions of the legislation. The excerpt is comparative analysis; it does not change the domestic governing law of those cases.
